value.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), let C denote the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg(W_1×W_2)=B_avg(W_1)+B_avg(W_2) for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBCs, even when the product-channel input law is correlated and the envelope auxiliary is joint across factors. If an involutive input relabeling exchanges the receivers, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products preserve this symmetry, so both scalar functionals are exactly additive on arbitrary finite products of receiver-skew-symmetric channels. For the half-skew BSSC P, using the accepted sharp one-letter BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture, B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) for every finite n≥1, with normalized value 0.3725562489182657... bits per channel use. This separately relaxed UV converse is non-frontier and does not change the governed capacity interval.

computations: Closed-form BSSC evaluation 2h_2(1/4)-5/4=0.3725562489182657... bits per use; supplied scripts provide only corroborative numerical and algebraic checks.

proofs: Analytic chain-rule factorization and concave-envelope argument proving exact additivity of B_avg for arbitrary finite-alphabet product channels with correlated inputs and joint envelope auxiliaries.
Envelope-covariance and concavity symmetrization proof showing B_br=B_avg under a receiver-exchanging involution and permitting restriction to invariant input laws.
Finite-product symmetry argument and half-skew BSSC specialization using the accepted sharp posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture.

value.title: Exact product and branchwise additivity of separately relaxed UV scalars

topologyRationale: A single leaf program is created under root for the shared activation event of investigating product or blocking gains in the two separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalars. It can be continued, stopped, or redirected independently of the existing code-induced support-reduction and channel-specific-refinement programs. No additional grouping parent is warranted because only one new accounting package is introduced. The averaged-product theorem, receiver-skew symmetry theorem, and BSSC specialization are not split into separate programs: they are theorem components serving the same blocking-converse decision, with the branchwise and BSSC conclusions depending on the averaged additivity chain. Extensions to nonsymmetric branchwise behavior or richer coupled UV systems remain residual work within the same coherent direction.
